text:
maria: heads up — we just saw a customer report where streaming reconnects are causing double billing for the same logical request. they reconnect during resume and get charged twice. :grimacing:

kai: ugh. is this the resume-id -> new-request mapping bug we talked about?

maria: looks like the gateway accepts the resumed session but creates a fresh usage record before resume verification completes. SDKs then push leftover tokens and both records show up in billing.

liam: can you paste an example header capture?

maria: example from capture:
```
GET /v1/stream?model=r-mod HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Client-Id: ui-12345
X-Resume-Id: r_9a3f
```

maria: after network flake client retries, server responds 200 on new connection and also resumes — two token receipts.

nora: telemetry question: do we have metrics keyed by X-Resume-Id today?

kai: no — resume-id only lives in request headers and isn't emitted to our usage pipeline. we only tag by request_id and route.

sam: from an ops/console POV we need to show reconnect churn per route so customers can triage. a simple reconnect-rate by client-id + model would help.

liam: proposal: (1) emit resume_id to usage/telemetry path, (2) de-dup usage events server-side for any resume_id seen within 30s, (3) add a dashboard tile for reconnect heatmap by route.

maria: +1 for resume_id in telemetry. de-duping window needs careful thought for long-running streams though. 30s might be too small if clients legitimately reconnect after a while.

kai: alternative: dedupe by (resume_id, request_signature) where request_signature is model+client_id+start_seq. if resume_id matches and signature matches then merge.

nora: to implement signals in the console we'll need an indexable field in our TSDB. can we call it streaming.resume_id?

liam: yes. we'll also add an event type streaming.reconnect with tags: route, model, client_id, resume_id, status_code.

sam: UX ask: show a hover that links reconnect bursts to sample request ids and a 'suppress duplicate billing' checkbox for enterprise customers while we roll this out.

maria: billing-side: we should avoid retroactive credits if we can prevent duplicates upstream. server-side suppression on identical resume_id within same model+client should be safe.

kai: implementation detail: gateway currently assigns a new internal_usage_id before auth finishes. move assignment after resume validation or include resume_id as parent_id when present.

liam: small patch idea:
```
if (headers.resume_id) {
  usage.parent = headers.resume_id;
} else {
  usage.parent = generate_new_id();
}
```

maria: also need to update the billing consumer to collapse usage where parent matches.

nora: alerting: create an alert for when reconnect_rate > 1% of streams for a route for > 5m. link to the new dashboard.

sam: rollout plan: feature-flag telemetry emission first, then enable server-side dedupe behind a flag, then expose console toggles. canary 10% traffic for 48h.

kai: one more edge: opaque proxies can strip custom headers. need a fallback — embed resume_id in a small signed cookie or in query param with short TTL.

maria: agreed. also document SDK behaviour: if resume_id absent, don't issue a retry that could cause duplication.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-09-stream-dup-billing linked by maria — https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-09

liam: I'll open the telemetry PR and add tests for parent collapsing. assigning to @kai for gateway changes and @nora for dashboard tiles.

kai: got it, starting a draft RFC for header + cookie fallback and dedupe semantics.

maria: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 11am to align rollout. :thumbsup:
